cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Transverse sinus

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Runs laterally from the confluence of sinuses along the attached margin of the tentorium cerebelli.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Receives blood from the confluence of sinuses and drains into the sigmoid sinus.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies in a groove of the occipital and temporal bones along the tentorial attachment.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sigmoid sinus

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Continuation of the transverse sinus; curves inferomedially in an S-shaped groove toward the jugular foramen.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Continues as the internal jugular vein at the jugular foramen.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies in the sigmoid sulcus of temporal and occipital bones.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior petrosal sinus

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Runs along the superior border of the petrous temporal bone in the attached margin of the tentorium cerebelli.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Connects the cavernous sinus with the transverse-sigmoid sinus junction.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Closely related to the trigeminal root and petrous ridge.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior petrosal sinus

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Runs in the petro-occipital fissure from the cavernous sinus toward the jugular foramen.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Drains the cavernous sinus into the internal jugular vein.

cards.question: Note
cards.answer: On one physical model, labels 4 and 6 are swapped; verify the structure rather than relying on the printed number alone.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Cavernous sinus

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Paired dural venous sinus on either side of the sella turcica.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Receives ophthalmic veins and superficial middle cerebral vein; drains via superior and inferior petrosal sinuses and emissary connections.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Internal carotid artery and abducens nerve pass within the sinus; CN III, IV, V1 and V2 run in the lateral wall.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Infection can spread from the face or orbit to cause cavernous sinus thrombosis with multiple cranial neuropathies.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Intercavernous sinus

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Venous channels connecting the right and left cavernous sinuses across the midline around the pituitary gland.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides communication between the paired cavernous sinuses.

cards.question: Note
cards.answer: On one physical model, labels 4 and 6 are swapped; verify the structure rather than relying on the printed number alone.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Occipital sinus

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Runs in the attached margin of the falx cerebelli along the internal occipital crest.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Communicates superiorly with the confluence of sinuses and inferiorly with the marginal sinus/internal vertebral venous plexus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Internal carotid artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal continuation of the common carotid artery after its bifurcation in the neck.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Enters the carotid canal, traverses the petrous temporal bone, passes through the cavernous sinus region, then enters the subarachnoid space.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Major intracranial branches include ophthalmic, posterior communicating, anterior choroidal, anterior cerebral and middle cerebral arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Major arterial supply to the anterior cerebral circulation and orbit.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ophthalmic artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually arises from the internal carotid artery after it leaves the cavernous sinus.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Enters the orbit through the optic canal with the optic nerve.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Includes central retinal, lacrimal, ciliary, supraorbital, ethmoidal and other orbital branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Orbit, retina, forehead, scalp and parts of the nasal cavity.

cards.question: Note
cards.answer: May not be present on all versions of the model.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Missing

cards.question: Note
cards.answer: No structure is provided for label 10 in the supplied guide.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Posterior communicating artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Branch of the internal carotid artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs posteriorly to join the posterior cerebral artery.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Forms part of the cerebral arterial circle (Circle of Willis), linking anterior and posterior circulations.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Posterior cerebral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of the basilar artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Curves around the midbrain toward the occipital and inferomedial temporal regions.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Occipital lobe, inferomedial temporal lobe and deep structures via perforating branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Basilar artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Formed by union of the vertebral arteries at the pontomedullary junction.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends in the basilar groove on the ventral surface of the pons.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Gives pontine branches, AICA, labyrinthine artery often via AICA, superior cerebellar arteries and terminates as posterior cerebral arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Brainstem, cerebellum and posterior cerebral circulation through its branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Basilar artery near its termination.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes laterally around the midbrain below the oculomotor nerve.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Superior cerebellum, superior cerebellar peduncle and parts of the rostral brainstem.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Labyrinthine artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually arises from the anterior inferior cerebellar artery, sometimes directly from the basilar artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Enters the internal acoustic meatus with CN VII and VIII.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Inner ear structures.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Basilar artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes laterally around the lower pons toward the cerebellopontine angle.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Anteroinferior cerebellum and lateral caudal pons; may give rise to the labyrinthine artery.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vertebral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: First part of the subclavian artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends through transverse foramina, enters the skull via foramen magnum and joins the opposite vertebral artery to form the basilar artery.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Gives posterior inferior cerebellar, anterior spinal, posterior spinal and medullary branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Medulla, spinal cord, cerebellum and posterior circulation through branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Anterior spinal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Formed by branches from the vertebral arteries.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends in the anterior median fissure of the spinal cord.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Anterior two-thirds of the spinal cord.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Vertebral artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Winds around the medulla toward the inferior cerebellum.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Posteroinferior cerebellum and lateral medulla.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Occlusion classically causes lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Middle meningeal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually a branch of the maxillary artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Enters the cranial cavity through foramen spinosum and runs between dura and inner skull.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Dura mater and calvarial structures.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Vulnerable near the pterion; rupture can cause an epidural haematoma.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Diploic vein

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Runs within the diploë of cranial bones.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Communicates with dural venous sinuses, emissary veins and extracranial veins.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Provides potential pathways for spread of infection between extracranial and intracranial venous systems.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Diploë

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Spongy cancellous bone between the inner and outer tables of flat cranial bones.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Contains marrow spaces and diploic veins.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Reduces skull weight while maintaining strength and houses venous channels.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Olfactory bulb

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Receives primary olfactory afferents from the nasal olfactory epithelium and begins central processing of smell.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies on the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone beneath the frontal lobe.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Olfactory tract (CN I)

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Extends posteriorly from the olfactory bulb along the inferior surface of the frontal lobe.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Conveys olfactory information from the bulb toward primary olfactory cortical areas.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Damage can cause anosmia; cribriform plate injury may disrupt olfactory fibres.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Optic nerve (CN II)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Special sensory fibres from retinal ganglion cells; functionally a CNS tract.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Leaves the orbit through the optic canal and reaches the optic chiasm.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Vision.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Lesion causes ipsilateral monocular visual loss and an afferent pupillary defect.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Oculomotor nerve (CN III)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Midbrain nuclei at the level of the superior colliculus; somatic motor and parasympathetic fibres.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Emerges from ventral midbrain, passes between posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries, travels in cavernous sinus wall and enters orbit via superior orbital fissure.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies superior, medial and inferior recti, inferior oblique and levator palpebrae superioris; parasympathetic fibres constrict pupil and accommodate.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Ptosis, 'down and out' eye, diplopia and possibly a dilated poorly reactive pupil.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Trochlear nerve (CN IV)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Trochlear nucleus in midbrain at level of inferior colliculus.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Only cranial nerve to emerge dorsally from brainstem; wraps around midbrain, runs in cavernous sinus wall and enters orbit through superior orbital fissure.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies superior oblique muscle.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes vertical diplopia, worse when looking down and in; patient may tilt head away from affected side.

cards.question: Note
cards.answer: May not be labelled on all versions of the model.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Trigeminal nerve (CN V)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Large sensory root and smaller motor root emerging from lateral pons.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Sensory root expands into trigeminal ganglion; divisions V1, V2 and V3 leave via superior orbital fissure, foramen rotundum and foramen ovale respectively.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Motor fibres travel with V3 to muscles of mastication and selected first-arch muscles.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Major somatic sensory nerve of face, cornea, nasal/oral cavities, teeth and much of cranial dura.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: May cause ipsilateral facial sensory loss; motor root involvement causes weakness of mastication with the jaw deviating toward the side of the lesion on opening; the corneal reflex afferent limb may be impaired if V1 is involved.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Trigeminal ganglion

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Lies in Meckel's cave near the apex of the petrous temporal bone.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Contains sensory neuron cell bodies of the trigeminal nerve.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Gives rise to ophthalmic (V1), maxillary (V2) and mandibular (V3) divisions.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ophthalmic branch of trigeminal nerve (CN V1)

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and exits the skull through the superior orbital fissure.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Sensation from cornea, upper eyelid, forehead, scalp, dorsum of nose and parts of nasal cavity and cranial dura.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: None; purely sensory.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Sensory loss in V1 territory and reduced/absent afferent limb of corneal reflex.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Maxillary branch of trigeminal nerve (CN V2)

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and exits via foramen rotundum into the pterygopalatine fossa.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Sensation from midface, upper lip, maxillary teeth, palate and parts of nasal cavity.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: None; purely sensory.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes sensory loss or paraesthesia over the midface, upper lip, maxillary teeth and palate; there is no motor deficit because V2 is purely sensory.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Mandibular branch of trigeminal nerve (CN V3)

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Exits cranial cavity through foramen ovale.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies muscles of mastication, mylohyoid, anterior belly of digastric, tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Sensation from lower face, mandibular teeth, anterior two-thirds of tongue for general sensation and parts of external ear and dura.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes sensory loss over the lower face, mandibular teeth and general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue; motor involvement weakens mastication and the jaw deviates toward the affected side on opening.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Abducens nerve (CN VI)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Abducens nucleus in caudal pons.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Emerges at pontomedullary junction, ascends over clivus, passes through cavernous sinus beside internal carotid artery and enters orbit via superior orbital fissure.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies lateral rectus muscle, abducting the eye.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes failure of abduction and horizontal diplopia; affected eye rests relatively medially.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Intermediate nerve of the facial nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Nervus intermedius carries sensory and parasympathetic fibres associated with CN VII.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Travels with the motor root of facial nerve through the internal acoustic meatus and facial canal.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Carries taste from anterior two-thirds of tongue and a small amount of somatic sensation from the ear.

cards.question: Parasympathetic functions
cards.answer: Carries preganglionic parasympathetic fibres for lacrimal, submandibular, sublingual and nasal/palatal glands.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Depending on the lesion level, may cause loss of taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and reduced lacrimal, submandibular and sublingual gland secretion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Facial nerve (CN VII)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Motor nucleus of facial nerve in pons, with sensory/parasympathetic fibres travelling in nervus intermedius.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Enters internal acoustic meatus, traverses facial canal, exits stylomastoid foramen and branches within parotid gland.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Muscles of facial expression, stapedius, stylohyoid and posterior belly of digastric.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Taste from anterior two-thirds of tongue; small somatic sensory component from external ear.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Lower motor neuron lesion causes ipsilateral weakness of upper and lower facial muscles; other deficits depend on lesion level.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Cochlear and vestibular divisions entering the brainstem at the cerebellopontine angle.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through internal acoustic meatus with CN VII.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Hearing via cochlear division and balance/head movement via vestibular division.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Can cause sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo and imbalance.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Medullary nuclei including nucleus ambiguus, inferior salivatory nucleus and nucleus solitarius pathways.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Emerges from postolivary sulcus and exits skull through jugular foramen.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies stylopharyngeus.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: General/taste sensation from posterior third of tongue, pharyngeal sensation and carotid body/sinus afferents.

cards.question: Parasympathetic functions
cards.answer: Secretomotor pathway to parotid gland via otic ganglion.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: May cause loss of taste and sensation from the posterior third of the tongue, impaired swallowing, loss of the afferent limb of the gag reflex and reduced parotid secretion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vagus nerve (CN X)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Medullary nuclei including nucleus ambiguus, dorsal motor nucleus of vagus and nucleus solitarius pathways.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Emerges from postolivary sulcus, exits through jugular foramen and descends in carotid sheath into thorax and abdomen.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies most muscles of palate, pharynx and larynx.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Visceral sensation from thoracoabdominal organs and sensation from larynx/pharynx; taste from epiglottic region.

cards.question: Parasympathetic functions
cards.answer: Parasympathetic supply to thoracic and much of abdominal viscera.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: May cause dysphagia and hoarseness, ipsilateral palatal weakness with the uvula deviating away from the lesion, and loss of the efferent limb of the gag reflex.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Accessory nerve (CN XI)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Spinal rootlets from upper cervical spinal cord, classically C1–C5/6.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Spinal root ascends through foramen magnum and exits skull through jugular foramen.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes weak head turning away from affected side and shoulder droop/weak shrug on affected side.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Hypoglossal nucleus in medulla.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Emerges between pyramid and olive and exits through hypoglossal canal.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies intrinsic and extrinsic tongue muscles except palatoglossus.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Lower motor neuron lesion causes ipsilateral tongue weakness, atrophy and deviation toward the lesion on protrusion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Cervical nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Arises from a cervical spinal nerve level; exact level is not specified in the supplied guide.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Carries somatic motor, sensory and autonomic fibres according to the specific cervical spinal nerve involved.

cards.question: Note
cards.answer: The supplied guide labels this generically as 'cervical nerve' without specifying a root level.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pituitary gland (hypophysis)

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Lies in the hypophyseal fossa of the sella turcica and connects to the hypothalamus via the infundibulum.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis) and posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis).

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Regulates multiple endocrine axes through secretion or release of hormones controlling growth, thyroid, adrenal, gonadal, lactational and water-balance functions.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Optic chiasm lies superiorly, sphenoidal sinus inferiorly and cavernous sinuses laterally.
